HIGHLIGHTS OF THE NOON BRIEFING BY STEPHANE DUJARRIC

SPOKESMAN FOR SECRETARY-GENERAL ANTÓNIO GUTERRES

TUESDAY, 25 AUGUST 2026

 

SECURITY COUNCIL/SECRETARY-GENERAL

This morning, the Secretary-General addressed the Security Council on conflict and food security. 

He said that critical food systems, and the lives and livelihoods they sustain, are under attack, pointing to farmers driven from their fields in the Sahel, markets hit by drone strikes and missiles in Sudan, and communities cut off by gang violence in Haiti. 

He noted that 2025 saw the highest number of armed conflicts since the Second World War alongside some of the highest levels of acute hunger on record. It was also the first time this century that two famines were confirmed simultaneously, in Sudan and in Gaza, which he described as a shameful milestone.

The Secretary-General called on the Council to implement Resolution 2417 in full, to protect food systems in their entirety, and to protect humanitarian workers.

Carl Skau, the Acting Executive Director of the World Food Programme, also briefed the Council. Speaking after his visit to Somalia last week, he warned that famine is getting closer there and stressed that waiting for famine to be declared is a total failure of duty.  

SOUTH SUDAN

Our colleagues at the Mission in South Sudan tell us that in the immediate aftermath of the attack [on peacekeepers in Jonglei State that occurred yesterday], the Mission deployed a quick reaction force by road and evacuated the injured by air. All those injured are receiving the medical attention they need and are currently stable.

Yesterday, a statement was issued in which the Secretary-General condemned the ambush by unidentified armed individuals.

He reminds that attacks against United Nations peacekeepers may constitute war crimes. All attacks on peacekeepers must be promptly investigated, and those responsible must be effectively prosecuted and held accountable.

UN RELIEF AND WORKS AGENCY FOR PALESTINE REFUGEES 

The Secretary-General condemns in the strongest terms today’s actions by the Israeli authorities, including its security forces, to unlawfully enter and remain in the UNRWA Kalandia Training Centre in occupied East Jerusalem and to carry out unauthorized works in those premises.

The Secretary-General is greatly alarmed by this development, as it will deprive young people of the vocational education they were receiving.

For over 70 years, the Centre has supported thousands of Palestine refugees through vocational education and a pathway to work.

Today’s actions are the fifth instance of unauthorized entry by the Israeli authorities into the Centre since May this year and follow other unacceptable breaches of the inviolability and interference with UN Relief And Works Agency For Palestine Refugees (UNRWA) premises in occupied East Jerusalem, including the seizure and demolition of the Sheikh Jarrah compound, as well as the cutting off the supply of water and electricity to multiple UNRWA facilities. These incidents take place in the context of domestic legislation which significantly impedes UNRWA from fulfilling the mandate in the Occupied Palestine Territory entrusted to it by the UN General Assembly. The Secretary-General reiterates the call for the repeal of the legislation.

The Kalandia Training Centre and other UNRWA premises are premises of the United Nations. They are inviolable and immune from any form of interference. 

These actions against UNRWA premises are wholly unacceptable and inconsistent with Israel’s clear obligations under international law, including the Charter of the UN and the Convention on the Privileges and Immunities of the United Nations. The International Court of Justice, in its Advisory Opinion of 22 October 2025, confirmed that with regard to the premises of the UN in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, Israel must respect their inviolability and not interfere with the performance of their functions.

The Secretary-General urges the Government of Israel to immediately cease the interference with UNRWA premises, vacate, return and restore all affected premises to the UN without delay, and protect those premises from further interference or damage. 

There was a message in the similar vein from the Special Coordinator ad interim, Dr. Ramiz Alakbarov. This was UNRWA’s oldest vocational training center. It has served people for more than seven decades. Each year, it provides hundreds of students from across the occupied West Bank with free vocational education and a pathway towards greater economic independence.

OCCUPIED PALESTINIAN TERRITORY

U.N. humanitarian partners shared that according to witnesses, the factory damaged in the Ramallah area, on the West Bank, was set on fire by Israeli settlers. The fire caused extensive damage to stored materials and the structure itself, and to nearby farmland. The U.N. and its partners are mobilizing humanitarian support for those affected by the incident.

This year, an average of over 200 attacks every month by Israeli settlers causing casualties and damage have been recorded, this is the highest monthly average in any year. By the end of July, more than 1,400 such attacks had been recorded.

In the wake of these attacks, U.N. humanitarian partners assess people’s needs and respond accordingly, including to support those who are forced to leave their communities and whose access to essential services and livelihoods is disrupted.

Meanwhile U.N. staff on the ground in Gaza reports that air strikes and other attacks on civilian areas in the Strip intensified yesterday, with reports of casualties, including among civilians, as well as damage.

Four of yesterday’s air strikes hit close to humanitarian facilities: in Shati’ Camp, in Al Bureij, and two locations in Deir al-Balah. Initial assessments indicate that the UN facilities were not damaged, but windows at a guesthouse used by some of our humanitarian partners were damaged.

On Sunday, an air strike damaged three UN warehouses. Supplies stored inside remained intact.

Civilians and civilian objects, including humanitarian facilities, must never be a target by anyone.

LEBANON

The U.N. Interim Force In Lebanon (UNIFIL)reports that from Friday to Monday, peacekeepers continued to observe significant Israeli land and air activities across their area of operations, including 173 airspace violations, mostly by drones, but also fighter jets.

Peacekeepers observed 51 instances of drone activity, including several drones operating in the vicinity of UN operations. One suicide drone overflew the main gate at a U.N. position before exploding approximately about 550 meters away. No casualties or material damage at the position have been reported.

UNIFIL peacekeepers detected 10 airstrikes by the Israeli Defense Forces (IDF) between Friday and Monday, including near Al Mansuri and other areas.

Also detected 668 trajectories of projectiles fired from the IDF from south to north, during that period.

They continue to record demolitions and infrastructure done by the Israeli armed forces in UNIFIL’s area of operations. On Monday, two detonations northwest of Al Mansuri, caused structural and collateral damage to a nearby UN position there. Thankfully, no peacekeeper casualties were reported.

On the same day, UNIFIL recorded aggressive behavior toward peacekeepers near Yatar, where local people on mopeds struck UN vehicles. No casualties or equipment damage were reported.

There were also multiple denials of freedom of movement involving the IDF during the reporting period.

Explosive and other potentially hazardous items continued to pose a threat to peacekeepers and of course to civilians in the area. On Saturday, UNIFIL peacekeepers discovered an unexploded ordnance along a road, southeast of Houla, which was neutralized on-site.

UN peacekeepers must never be targeted. They are there to support peace and protect civilians, as mandated by the Security Council, and must be allowed to carry out their work safely.

Meanwhile, UNIFIL continues to support humanitarian access in southern Lebanon in coordination with the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA).

HAITI

The Secretary-General condemns the latest gang attack that was witnessed on Kenscoff, a commune on the outskirts of the capital of Haiti, Port-au-Prince. This attack reportedly killed at least 47 people during the night of 23 August, including 22 who were reportedly executed in a church compound where they had sought safety.

The relentless attacks on communities and the loss of lives underscore the alarming security conditions in Haiti and reinforce the urgent need to intensify Haitian and international security efforts to counter these ruthless gangs.

The Secretary-General reiterates his call for Haitian authorities to ensure that those responsible for such attacks are held to account, including through the specialized judicial units, recently created with international support to investigate mass crimes.

U.N. staff on the ground in Haiti is working with the local communities and local authorities to verify the information and assess what people need following this horrendous violence.

The U.N. Integrated Office in Haiti (BINUH), reported that during the second quarter of 2026, from April to June, at least 1,408 people were killed and 656 others injured because of violence across Haiti. Gang attacks accounted for more than half of all killings, injuries recorded during the quarter.

The report emphasizes the importance of keeping Haiti on the international agenda and accelerating the full deployment of the Gang Suppression Force. It also calls for progress on investigations into mass crimes and reiterates that all use of force by law enforcement officials, or other actors acting on behalf of the State, must comply with international human rights law.

UKRAINE

The U.N. Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs informs that attacks and hostilities have taken a heavy toll on civilians in recent days. According to local authorities, at least 47 people were killed and 329 injured. That includes children, and that was between Friday and the early hours of today.

One of the deadliest incidents was a so called double-tap attack on a busy shopping mall in Kryvyi Rih, in the Dnipro region. Matthias Schmale, the Humanitarian Coordinator in Ukraine, condemned the attack and reiterated that civilians must always be protected under international humanitarian law.  

Civilian casualties were also reported in Chernihiv City, and in Donetsk, Dnipro, Kharkiv, Kherson, Sumy and Zaporizhzhia, where homes, a school, shops, vehicles and other civilian infrastructure were damaged.   

All of this continues to put vital aid operations at risk. On Sunday, a drone attack caused a fire at a Ukrainian Red Cross Society warehouse in Kherson, damaging or destroying supplies worth more than half a million US dollars. 

Thankfully, no one was injured.

Despite the dangers, the U.N., along with its humanitarian partners, continue to respond. Following the attack in Kryvyi Rih, aid workers immediately mobilized at the site and in hospitals to support people in need. Humanitarian organizations provided families with as much as they could.

SECURITY COUNCIL/UKRAINE
Yesterday, Rosemary Di Carlo, Under Secretary-General Political and Peacebuilding Affairs, briefed the Security Council on Ukraine. Noting that four and half years after the full-scale invasion began, the need to end this war could not be more urgent.

Also briefing was Tom Fletcher, Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief Coordinator, who noted that during the time he recently spent in Ukraine, he witnessed the impact of drone warfare.

Technology is now outpacing accountability, he said, warning that abandon the rules of war and we all face the chilling reality the Ukrainians face right now.

SECRETARY-GENERAL/INTERNATIONAL COMMITTEE OF THE RED CROSS - AUTONOMOUS WEAPONS SYSTEMS

Today, the Secretary-General and the President of the International Committee of the Red Cross, Mirjana Spoljaric, issued a renewed call for States to adopt new international rules on autonomous weapon systems. This joint appeal follows a similar call they issued three years ago.

Since the appeal, States have laid important groundwork through the General Assembly and the Group of Governmental Experts under the Convention on Certain Types of Conventional Weapons. However, weapon technology has continued to advance at a rapid pace, placing increasing strain on existing legal frameworks. The Secretary-General and the President of the ICRC warn that we are dangerously close to crossing what they describe as a moral red line: allowing machines to autonomously set a target on human beings.

They urge States to negotiate a legally binding instrument establishing clear prohibition and restriction on autonomous weapon systems, stressing that the progress achieved over the past three years should not be lost. The Seventh Review Conference of the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons, will be held in November, that is an opportunity to move the work forward.

ROHINGYA

The Secretary-General issued a statement on the nine years since the forced mass displacement of Rohingya and other communities from Myanmar. He called for renewed global attention and action to the plight of the Rohingyas, noting that Rohingya people in Myanmar, Bangladesh and across the region face deepening insecurity, shrinking protection and diminishing prospects for durable solutions, worsened by funding cuts impacting life-saving assistance.

He also underscored that he appreciates the hospitality of Bangladesh and other refugee-hosting nations.

DEPUTY SECRETARY-GENERAL/TRAVELS   

The Deputy Secretary-General, Amina J. Mohammed, continued her engagements in Ulaanbaatar, at the 17th session of the Conference of the Parties to the U.N. Convention to Combat Desertification. She participated in the Dialogue on Accelerating Drought Resilience, where she urged countries to turn early warnings into early action, supported by anticipatory measures and adequate financing.

The Deputy Secretary-General also took part in a High-Level Event on Sand and Dust Storms, which saw the launch of the SG’s Framework for the UN Decade on Combating Sand and Dust Storms.

And she also met on the sidelines with African leaders, heads of delegations, as well as UN country team. She has since departed Mongolia for India.

SUDAN

The Humanitarian and Resident Coordinator, Denise Brown, expressed deep concern over the situation in Heiban, in South Kordofan, where the conflict between non-state armed groups continues to take a heavy toll on civilians, leading to displacement and the destruction of critical civilian infrastructure.

In a statement she said that the arbitrary detention of humanitarian personnel and the looting and destruction of humanitarian compounds, supplies and equipment are disrupting life-saving operations and depriving people of critical assistance.

She urged all parties again to protect civilians and to respect international humanitarian law.

SPOKESPERSON’S OFFICE/STAFF

Inazio Lopez Ochoa and Nadia Al-Kabariti joined the Spokesperson’s Office.

Inazio comes from the Department of Global Communications. He brings over nine years of experience in public information and journalism. Before joining the UN, he spent five years as a journalist working in Spain, at Basque Public Television, reporting on national and international news.

Nadia brings experience in strategic communications, digital partnerships across humanitarian, media, and development settings. She has worked and studied in a number of countries, including her native Jordan, in Geneva, and in Vienna. 

Stephanie Tremblay has received a well-deserved promotion and has moved on to the Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs, for at least a year where she'll be working on communications issues. 

Stephanie has been a pillar of stability and efficiency in the Spokesperson’s Office. We will miss her.

FINANCIAL CONTRIBUTION

Mozambique paid their dues to the regular budget today. There are now 130 fully paid-up Member States.
